purpose: Microsoft Azure Logic Apps and Power Automate documentation promotion with workflow-run plus downstream-delivery reconciliation.

overrides.reason: Promote the existing Microsoft integration target to documentation-backed, read-only workflow-run and downstream-delivery reconciliation without granting resubmit, cancellation, workflow, connection, checkpoint, payroll or attendance authority.

connectionRoutes: Azure Resource Manager read APIs over the exact public Azure management origin with a least-privilege Microsoft Entra principal
Consumption workflow management routes under Microsoft.Logic API version 2019-05-01
Standard workflow management routes under Microsoft.Web App Service API version 2026-03-15
Managed identities for supported workflow connections to Microsoft Entra-protected Azure resources
On-premises data gateway or Standard Hybrid as separately governed customer-edge routes
Power Automate cloud flow history as a separately governed Power Platform environment route
readRoutes: GET workflow runs and one exact workflow run
GET workflow run actions with documented nextLink pagination
GET workflow run action request histories where explicitly approved
Read-only workflow and connection metadata needed to bind definition and connection-set fingerprints
Power Automate run history and Dataverse FlowRun metadata where customer policy and licensing permit
deniedMutationRoutes: resubmit, cancel, enable, disable, start or delete workflow runs
create, update or delete workflows, triggers, actions, connections, custom connectors, gateways or integration accounts
edit workflow definitions or environment variables
source-system, downstream-system, schedule, payroll or attendance mutations
stableIds: Microsoft Entra tenant plus Azure subscription
resource group plus Logic App resource plus workflow name
opaque workflow run name and action name
WFM tenant plus connection plus dataset plus source-scope fingerprint
patch.freshness: Preserve provider run/action start and end times, the WFM observation horizon and a later downstream delivery timestamp. A provider Succeeded state is never treated as source completeness or checkpoint authority.
permissions: Use Logic Apps Standard Reader or a narrower custom read role for Standard run history
Use a least-privilege Azure Resource Manager read principal isolated per customer tenant, subscription and workflow scope
Do not grant Operator, Developer, Contributor, resubmit, cancellation, workflow-editing, connection-secret or gateway-administration privileges to the WFM read path
Secure or omit workflow inputs and outputs because run history can expose sensitive customer data
paginationAndDelta: Workflow run-action list responses expose nextLink and value arrays; reconcile one gapless terminal cursor-fingerprint chain
Bind one exact run name, workflow definition fingerprint and approved action-name set
Require every approved action to be present exactly once and Succeeded
Require a separately produced successful complete downstream delivery receipt for the same run, delivery action, payload digest, dataset, schema, mapping, source scope and closed source window
Power Automate and Logic Apps history retention is not a durable source checkpoint; preserve governed WFM evidence before provider expiry
patch.customFields: Workflow action names, tracking identifiers, connector configuration and customer expressions are deployment-specific. WFM stores only approved bounded identifiers and fingerprints; raw action inputs, outputs, secrets and arbitrary expressions remain excluded.
regionalAndVersionNotes: Bind the exact customer-selected Azure tenant, subscription, resource group, region and hosting model
Standard, Consumption, App Service Environment, Hybrid and Power Automate routes remain separate authorities
Standard data stays in the selected deployment region, while connector and paired-region behavior must be checked for the customer's exact design
Multi-region disaster recovery requires separately deployed workflows, connections, gateways and dependent resources; never collapse primary and secondary run identities
Preserve customer-chosen WFM residency and cross-border transfer policy independently of the provider deployment
patch.rateLimits: No universal safe request rate is assumed. Honour HTTP throttling and Retry-After, provider and connector concurrency limits, bounded page/action caps and environment-specific Power Platform allocations. Stop on tenant, subscription, region, workflow definition, connection-set, schema or permission drift.
failureModes: expired or revoked Microsoft Entra credentials and insufficient RBAC
wrong tenant, subscription, resource group, region, hosting model, Logic App resource or workflow
Running, Waiting, Skipped, Suspended, Cancelled, Failed, Faulted, TimedOut, Aborted or Ignored run/action states
incomplete, repeated, conflicting, looping or nonterminal action pagination
missing, duplicate, unexpected or failed approved actions
run/action timestamps outside the closed source window or observation horizon
workflow Succeeded without a later successful complete downstream delivery receipt
delivery dataset, action, digest, record count, schema, mapping, source scope or source window mismatch
connector throttling, a continuously throttled Power Automate flow being turned off, gateway outage or regional partial outage
run history exposing raw credentials, tokens, personal data or unapproved payloads
reconciliation: Bind every receipt to the exact WFM tenant, connection, Azure tenant, subscription, resource group, region, hosting model, Logic App resource and workflow
Pin management API version, principal, workflow definition, connection set, dataset schema, mapping and source scope fingerprints
Require one Succeeded run and a complete terminal action-page chain containing the exact approved action set once
Require a later independently produced complete downstream delivery receipt bound to the delivery action payload digest and closed source window
Emit only an integration-delivery reconciliation candidate; durable checkpoint movement remains a later compare-and-swap decision
patch.schemaDrift: Pin hosting model, API version, workflow definition, connection set, approved action set, management response schema, dataset schema and mapping fingerprints. Quarantine new statuses, action names, routes, connector variants, missing tracking fields or changed pagination semantics.
retryAndRecovery: Retry read-only management queries with bounded exponential backoff and Retry-After handling
Do not use provider run resubmit as automated data recovery because it can repeat source or downstream side effects
After connection, gateway or regional recovery, observe a distinct new run and repeat downstream-delivery reconciliation
Recover missed provider history from the authoritative source window when still available; otherwise require a governed source snapshot or backfill

patch.evidenceNote: Official Microsoft documentation was reachable on 2026-09-27 and supports Consumption and Standard workflow management routes, run/action states, nextLink pagination, Microsoft Entra/RBAC and managed-identity security, regional and on-premises variants, limits, disaster recovery and Power Automate environment constraints. No Azure subscription, Power Platform environment, customer authentication, live workflow read, downstream delivery, denied mutation, gateway outage, regional failover, hosted proof or production certification was executed.
valueOpportunities: Reuse existing customer workflows across ERP, HCM, payroll, MES, maintenance, quality, inventory, logistics and finance instead of building duplicate point-to-point connectors
Detect workflow-Succeeded but incompletely delivered data before schedules, payroll preparation or operational decisions consume it
Separate workflow, connector, gateway, throttling and downstream-delivery failures to shorten diagnosis and recovery
Preserve workflow/run/action identifiers and source windows for implementation evidence, freshness diagnostics and outcome lineage
Support small customers through one low-configuration workflow and global enterprises through isolated tenants, subscriptions, regions, hosting models, workflows, datasets and delegated owners
patch.nextBuildAction: In an authorised Azure Logic Apps non-production subscription, authenticate a least-privilege read principal, observe one exact Consumption or Standard workflow through Succeeded, enumerate its terminal action history, reconcile it to an immutable WFM delivery receipt, then exercise token expiry, throttling, failed/skipped actions, continuation gaps, workflow-definition drift and a deliberately incomplete delivery without resubmitting or mutating the workflow.
